paras: The police shooting of Dudley Singleton took place shortly after noon on Monday, 23 June 1919, when Patrolman Walker of Cleveland's E. 37th St. station shot Singleton, a Black man, in the left leg and abdomen during a fight in a Central Avenue poolroom. The Cleveland Gazette described the wounding as probably fatal, and a week later Singleton's name appeared on an undertakers' list in the Cleveland Advocate.

According to the Gazette, a "free-for-all fight" broke out in a poolroom at 4206 Central Ave. between Singleton and James Carey, the poolroom's proprietor. Patrolman Walker shot Singleton in the left leg and abdomen; by Walker's account, Singleton had attacked him while he was trying to act as peacemaker between the two men. The Gazette attributed that justification to Walker alone, adding "so says the officer."

Carey was taken to Charity hospital with injuries sustained in the fight, which the paper described as the "serious injury" of a second Black man. Singleton was taken to St. Luke's hospital, where he was reported in critical condition.

On 5 July the Cleveland Advocate printed a Slaughter Bros. undertakers' report that listed "Dudley Singleton, St. Luke's Hospital" as shipped to Milledgeville, Georgia. The list gave no cause of death and did not mention the shooting, so the link rests on the matching name and hospital. The coverage shows no inquest, hearing, or action against Patrolman Walker.

The shooting appeared in the Black press only as a short paragraph in the Cleveland Gazette's local-news column of 28 June, set between society items and a note on a quarrel between two pawnbrokers. The item carried no headline or editorial comment, though its closing attribution, "so says the officer," kept a distance from the patrolman's account. The Cleveland Advocate did not report the shooting itself; Singleton appeared there only as a name on a list of burials and shipments.

reader.title: Police shooting of Dudley Singleton
bases: A Cleveland patrolman, Walker of the E. 37th St. station, shot Dudley Singleton while intervening in a poolroom fight; no mob or crowd action against Singleton is reported (A1).
Only the Cleveland Gazette reported the shooting (A1); the Cleveland Advocate's undertakers' list (A2) bears only on Singleton's apparent death, not on how he was shot.

accounts.label: Officer's account (as relayed by the Cleveland Gazette)
accounts.gist: Patrolman Walker said he shot Singleton when Singleton attacked him as he tried to separate Singleton and Carey; the Gazette marked this as the officer's version.
